subject: Post-demo: targeted probe plan + competitive checks
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@dataforge.com>, Mike Chen <mike@dataforge.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: targeted probe plan + competitive checks

Hi Ellie / Mike —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciate the crisp questions on latency and data residency. Per our conversation, I’m proposing a short, tightly scoped probe run so your engineers can validate where Redwood sits versus the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned (HyperscalerX and CloudWave). Goal: baseline model quality (instruction-following & hallucination), latency at 99th pct, and per-unit cost for your typical legal-reasoning prompts.

Attached: dataforge-probes.csv (a starter set of 75 prompts covering instruction-following, closed-domain QA, and hallucination stress cases) and a baseline-metrics-template.xlsx to capture the outputs we’ll request. Suggested plan:
- Week 0 (this week): you run Redwood + HyperscalerX + CloudWave on a 75-prompt set, 3 seeds each (deterministic sampling disabled). Collect answer text + token counts + per-call latency.
- Week 1: Redwood team runs a matched evaluation with quantization-variant we discussed (int8 vs fp16) if you want a cost-oriented view.
- Deliverable: CSV with input/output pairs, a short table with hallucination flags (yes/no), 99th pct latency, and tokenized cost estimate.

Key probes to prioritize (short list to start):
1) Instruction-following with multi-step constraints (e.g., "summarize then extract dates and list as ISO dates only").
2) Closed-domain factual QA (docs + citations) to measure hallucination rates.
3) Ambiguous prompts to observe stability and temperature sensitivity (compare sampling settings).

We’ll also provide a one-page comparator that highlights where Redwood’s serving/runtime optimizations (KV cache reuse, continuous batching, fallback model variants) will typically move the cost/latency tradeoff relative to hyperscalers.

Can you confirm:
- Who on your side will run the initial sweep?
- Any data-sharing limits (no PII in prompts, masked docs ok)?
- A preferred deadline for the initial results (suggest Friday 11/20).

If useful I can set up a quick 30-min working session with our CS lead (Marissa) and PM (Aisha) to walk through the probes and metric collection.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: dataforge-probes.csv (75 prompts), baseline-metrics-template.xlsx (template for results)
From: Ellie Park <ellie@dataforge.com>

Cc: Mike Chen <mike@dataforge.com>, security@dataforge.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: targeted probe plan + competitive checks

Alex —

Appreciate the clear plan. Mike and I will run the initial sweep; I’ll own the run and coordinate with our infra lead (cc’d: security@dataforge.com for the data handling checklist). A couple of notes:
- Timeline: Friday 11/20 is tight but doable; can we extend to Monday 11/23 if we hit infra queueing?
- For HyperscalerX and CloudWave, we’ll use their standard generation endpoint with default sampling params, then a second run with temperature=0 to measure determinism.
- Can you confirm if Redwood’s suggested quantization run requires any model artifact from our side or we can request it through your hosted API?

Also, security asked for a short answer on data retention: do Redwood-hosted logs retain prompts? We’ll pass security follow-up to your team (if you could please loop in the security contact).

We’ll send a CSV with the results and a single sample report back to you.

—Ellie
Director of AI Integrations | DataForge
ellie@dataforge.com
